observations: Independently viewed all 12 final PNGs with view_image: baseline and candidate, stage and face crop, for native-adult-support, native-adult-support-before, and native-infant-support-contrast. Archived camera diagnostics were not used for acceptance.

Adult support: the candidate tip is visibly shallower and less pendant, with a gentler bridge-to-tip transition. The nose remains rounded and readable. This is a modest improvement at stage scale and clearer in the face crop.

Adult support before: the opposite head orientation also shows reduced tip prominence and a smoother bridge slope. The small nostril detail remains visible, and I see no new hole, detached edge, sharp ridge, or shading discontinuity.

Infant high contrast: the nasal contour remains legible against the white face in both stage and face images. The candidate contour is slightly shallower and smoother at the tip. No visible loss of the nose outline or nostril mark is introduced in the captured area.
The visible surrounding facial features and supporting hand remain consistent across each pair. Acceptance is based on the rendered shape and shading in these images, not on changed-pixel counts.
limitations: Raw-module render review only; the full app build and module-loading path were not tested by this review. These are three fixed Supporting hand close-up views, so this does not establish behavior from every camera angle, pose, profile, or lighting setup. The infant high-contrast framing clips the outer head edge, and its small monochrome nose supports a limited contour-readability judgment rather than a detailed surface-shading assessment. The adult improvement is subtle at normal stage size. Camera and crop equality and nonvisual preservation checks were reported by the root agent; this reviewer independently inspected the images and computed the source and image hashes.
